analysis.session_summary: The session was a mild risk-on, USD-soft tape: SPX +73.4, VIX -52.3, BTC +2389.9 and gold +233.2 while DXY lost -4.7 points. Commodity FX led via AUD/USD +28.5 pips and NZD/USD +12.5 pips, while EUR/USD +2.4 and GBP/USD +3.1 lagged. No leg had a clear news catalyst; the only measured event reaction, Unemployment Claims (203K vs 208K), was muted at 0.009% and failed to lift the dollar. Price action was range-bound with risk-on outperformance despite negative geopolitical headlines.

themes.evidence: SPX +73.4 at 1.0 close-in-range, VIX -52.3 at 0.0 close-in-range, BTC +2389.9, Gold +233.2, AUD/USD +28.5 and AUD/NZD +22.1.

themes.theme: Broad USD softness but euro/sterling lag
themes.evidence: DXY -4.7 points, USD/CHF -17.4 pips, USD/CAD -21.0 pips, USD/JPY -12.4 pips; EUR/USD +2.4 and GBP/USD +3.1 failed to extend.

themes.theme: Geopolitical headlines failed to leave a lasting footprint
themes.evidence: Hormuz tanker strike at 03:15, North Korea at 07:15, Kyiv explosion at 10:00 with no clear leg catalyst; SPX, BTC and gold still rallied.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: EUR/USD chopped through five legs from -18.8 to +19.3 with no clear catalyst, closing only +2.4 pips at 1.16521.
leg_notes.GBP/USD: GBP/USD's meaningful -20.9 decline from 09:00 to 14:45 had no clear catalyst, but a late +19.1 bounce left it +3.1 pips.
leg_notes.AUD/USD: AUD/USD built a +15.9 up leg, absorbed a -10.2 dip, then added +21.6 into the close, ending +28.5 pips at 0.71972 and 0.99 close-in-range.
leg_notes.NZD/USD: NZD/USD whipsawed 14.3 up, -17.2 down and 17.4 up with no clear drivers, finishing +12.5 pips.
leg_notes.USD/JPY: USD/JPY declined -27.2, recovered +34.5, then faded -19.2 without clear catalysts, closing -12.4 pips at 159.292.
leg_notes.USD/CHF: USD/CHF's largest move was a -27.1 drop from 10:15 to 15:15 with no clear catalyst, leaving it -17.4 pips.
leg_notes.USD/CAD: USD/CAD had a sharp -35.8 leg from 09:15 to 15:15, but no clear catalyst; it closed -21.0 pips at 1.38566.
leg_notes.EUR/CHF: EUR/CHF faded from a +16.0 up leg into a -26.6 decline with no clear catalyst, ending -18.3 pips.
leg_notes.CHF/JPY: CHF/JPY had the only measurable leg driver: BOJ Himino added 4.9 pips, 20% of one up leg, yet no full catalyst; it closed +27.5 pips.
leg_notes.AUD/NZD: AUD/NZD saw a -22.6 start, a +30.0 bounce, a -14.5 dip and a +30.5 grind, closing +22.1 pips near the high at 0.95 close-in-range.
leg_notes.EUR/GBP: EUR/GBP traded eight tiny no-news legs to finish just +0.1 pip at 0.8572.
leg_notes.AUD/CHF: AUD/CHF rallied +24.8 from 23:15 to 10:15 with no clear trigger, then faded a bit to +10.2 pips.
leg_notes.NZD/CHF: NZD/CHF alternated no-catalyst moves and closed almost flat at -0.3 pips.
leg_notes.USD/ZAR: USD/ZAR whipsawed -399.3, +842.9, -291.6 with no clear catalyst, finishing only +28.1 pips.
leg_notes.USD/MXN: USD/MXN had -195.1, +502.7, -208.5 no-news legs and closed +65.4 pips.
leg_notes.Gold/USD: Gold/USD rallied +458.8, fell -679.4, then bounced +422.0 with no clear news, closing +233.2 pips.
leg_notes.BTC/USD: BTC/USD extended +2362.1, corrected -1244.5, then reclaimed +1146.6, closing +2389.9 pips as the strongest risk bid.
leg_notes.Brent/USD: Brent/USD had a -203.0 decline and +238.3 bounce without clear catalysts, closing -1.5 pips.

polarity_reads.read: Actual 203K beat 208K forecast, but the own-currency impulse was only 0.009% with top mover GBP/USD at -0.027%; this muted response says the USD was already positioned soft and the data did not alter Jackson Hole/payrolls focus.

polarity_reads.event: BOJ Deputy Governor Himino: Weak Yen Drives Inflation Higher
polarity_reads.read: Not a full event reaction; only measurable contribution was +4.9 pips in CHF/JPY, 20% of that leg, suggesting the market discounted BOJ jawboning as a yen catalyst.

scenarios.name: Risk-on continuation
scenarios.thesis: Despite negative geopolitics, risk assets closed strong; AUD/USD close_in_range 0.99, SPX close_in_range 1.0, VIX close 0.0. If Warsh is not hawkish and the payroll benchmark stays deeply negative, commodity/risk longs extend.
triggers: Tokyo Core CPI y/y prints below 1.8%
Fed Chairman Warsh sounds balanced or dovish
Prelim Benchmark Payrolls Revision remains near -911K or worse
scenarios.invalidation: DXY recovers above 99.039 and AUD/USD loses 0.71972 on a hawkish USD catalyst.

pair_paths.rationale: Today's range; close near high supports extension.
Positive close_in_range at 0.73 with commodity strength.
Risk-on and CAD strength with Canada GDP ahead.
Gold already rebounded +422.0 into the close.

scenarios.name: USD hawkish repricing
scenarios.thesis: USD is the weakest currency at -0.156% and DXY closed -4.7 points; Fed Warsh and the payroll benchmark can trigger a short squeeze, especially if Warsh pushes back on easing or the benchmark is less negative than -911K.
triggers: Fed's Warsh highlights upside inflation risks
Prelim Benchmark Payrolls Revision prints less negative than -911K
Revised UoM Inflation Expectations remains at 4.3% or higher
scenarios.invalidation: AUD/USD holds above 0.71972 and DXY stays below 99.039 while Warsh avoids hawkish signals.

pair_paths.rationale: Today's range; pair vulnerable if USD reprices.
USD short squeeze; JPY only modestly stronger.
CHF strength reverses in a USD catch-up.
High-beta commodity long unwinds on USD squeeze.

scenarios.name: Range/chop awaiting Jackson Hole
scenarios.thesis: Market may stay in today's ranges with no hard catalyst before Jackson Hole; EUR/GBP was nearly flat at +0.1 pip and EUR/USD only +2.4 pips.
triggers: Warsh message falls in line with current pricing
scenarios.invalidation: A break of EUR/USD 23.2-pip range or USD/JPY 40.2-pip range on a calendar surprise.

pair_paths.rationale: Likely inside day after +3.1 pip session.

risks.risk: Geopolitical escalation in Hormuz, Korea, or Ukraine
risks.why_it_matters: These headlines were ignored today; VIX closed at 0.0 of range and SPX at 1.0 of range, so a genuine escalation would hit from a complacent base.

risks.risk: Hawkish Fed Warsh / less negative payroll benchmark
risks.why_it_matters: USD is the weakest currency at -0.156% and DXY closed -4.7 points; a Warsh hawkish surprise or benchmark better than -911K could force a USD short squeeze.
CAD strength is priced after USD/CAD fell -21.0 pips; GDP forecast 0.2% vs previous 0.3% could unwind CAD and lift USD/CAD.

analysis.calendar_ahead_note: Tokyo Core CPI y/y (01:30) forecast 1.8% vs 1.9% previous is the first JPY test; Canada GDP m/m (14:30) is 0.2% vs 0.3%; then Fed Chairman Warsh Speaks, Prelim Benchmark Payrolls Revision (previous -911K), Revised UoM Consumer Sentiment 51.0, Revised UoM Inflation Expectations 4.3%, and Jackson Hole Symposium at 18:15. The main repricing risk is a hawkish Warsh or a less negative payroll benchmark; otherwise the risk-on commodity bid likely holds into Jackson Hole.
